title: Oliver Coleman, teacher
summary: Jones praises Oliver Coleman, who taught more drummers than anyone, and recalls his last visit to him with cancer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: There was another great drummer around Chicago that we thought a lot of. I just wanted to ask you, did you ever run into Oliver Coleman?

Please, you know that was O.C., that was my friend and I gave him a secret and fortunately for him - it's rather difficult for a person to instruct and teach music at the same time and to have pupils that can come out and be a credit to him. Because you know you can go to Harvard, Dartmouth, and Yale. You can go to Eton. I don't care where you go. You can go anywhere in the world,

but you can't top your professor. But it's a credit that he has more pupils out here in the world than any drummer including Bishop, including Bertrand... including Cozy which is a wonderful instructor. Oliver Coleman, my very dear friend. I went to see Oliver Coleman when he had cancer and I said, "I'm on my way to California." It was the same year that Nat King Cole died. He would not go to bed. He insisted on getting up out of the bed and driving me to the hotel and getting me some barbecue. I couldn't make him go to bed. When I got to California his son came up and said, "Pop died."
Bob Rosengarten is one of his students.

Of course. You know, Bob when I was on 44th Street, he'd be down there with Steve Allen, Bob would run up and I'd say, what are you talking about? I'd say, go to Oliver. See, I gave Oliver a key. There's a lot of people wanted a key... this is something I can give to you. You're my friend. Because remember I came through Oliver when his claim to fame when I first met him was 3 or 4 quarts of whiskey a day. He wasn't married. To get him out of that, to get him married, and to take him to Wisdom 102 -
Where he became a Worshipful Master.
